statement: Select rectifier diodes with reverse-breakdown voltage at least 50% greater than the expected PIV of the topology. Expected PIV: half-wave PIV = Vs (peak secondary voltage); center-tapped full-wave PIV = 2Vs - VD; bridge PIV = Vs - VD (roughly half the center-tap case).
condition: Any diode rectifier (half-wave, center-tapped full-wave, or bridge) fed from a sinusoid of peak Vs, diode drop VD.
formula: V_breakdown >= 1.5 * PIV; PIV_halfwave = Vs; PIV_centertap = 2*Vs - VD; PIV_bridge = Vs - VD
erc_rule: For each rectifier diode: fail if diode V_RRM < 1.5 * PIV_expected, where PIV_expected is computed per topology from the formulas above.

statement: For a peak rectifier (filter capacitor C across load R), the peak-to-peak ripple is Vr = Vp/(fCR) for half-wave and Vr = Vp/(2fCR) for full-wave (ripple frequency is 2f for full-wave). Equivalently Vr = IL/(fC) with IL = Vp/R. Size C so that CR >> T to keep Vr small.
condition: Peak rectifier with CR >> T (period of input); approximation valid only while Vr << Vp.
formula: Vr = Vp/(f*C*R) [half-wave, Eq. 4.29a]; Vr = IL/(f*C) [Eq. 4.29b]; Vr = Vp/(2*f*C*R) [full-wave, Eq. 4.33]
erc_rule: Given target ripple Vr_max: fail if C < Vp/(Vr_max*f*R) for half-wave or C < Vp/(2*Vr_max*f*R) for full-wave.

source.section: 4.5.4 The Rectifier with a Filter Capacitor (Peak Rectifier)

statement: Classical single-supply voltage-divider BJT bias: design for VBB (base divider voltage) about 1/3 VCC, VCB (or VCE) about 1/3 VCC, and IC*RC about 1/3 VCC. Stability constraints: VBB >> VBE and RE >> RB/(beta+1). Choose R1, R2 so the divider current is in the range 0.1*IE to IE.
condition: Discrete BJT amplifier biased from a single supply VCC via base voltage divider R1/R2 with emitter resistor RE.
formula: VBB ~ VCC/3; VCE ~ VCC/3; IC*RC ~ VCC/3; 0.1*IE <= I_divider <= IE; VBB >> VBE; RE >> RB/(beta+1)
erc_rule: Flag if base-divider Thevenin voltage deviates far from VCC/3, if VCE drop is far from VCC/3, or if divider current VCC/(R1+R2) is below 0.1*IE (bias becomes beta-sensitive).

statement: Worked application of the one-third rule: for VCC = 12 V and target IE = 1 mA (beta = 100), allocate VB = +4 V, giving VE = 4 - VBE ~ 3.3 V, so RE = 3.3 kOhm; with divider current 0.1*IE = 0.1 mA, R1 + R2 = 120 kOhm, yielding R2 = 40 kOhm and R1 = 80 kOhm.
condition: Single-supply voltage-divider BJT bias, VCC = 12 V, IE = 1 mA, beta = 100.

statement: Classical MOSFET bias with drain resistor RD and source-degeneration resistor RS: choose RD and RS so that one-third of VDD drops across each of RD, the transistor (VDS), and RS. Book example: VDD = 15 V gives VD = +10 V and VS = +5 V; with ID = 0.5 mA, RD = RS = 10 kOhm.
condition: Discrete MOSFET amplifier biased by fixed gate voltage (divider) plus source resistance RS from supply VDD.
formula: V(RD) ~ VDD/3; VDS ~ VDD/3; V(RS) ~ VDD/3

values.example: VDD=15V -> VD=+10V, VS=+5V; ID=0.5mA -> RD=RS=10 kOhm

erc_rule: Flag if the drain-node or source-node DC voltages deviate substantially from 2*VDD/3 and VDD/3 respectively in a classical RD/RS-biased MOSFET stage.

statement: Wien-bridge oscillator (noninverting op amp, gain 1 + R2/R1, with series/parallel RC feedback): oscillation frequency is w0 = 1/(CR); oscillation requires R2/R1 = 2 for unity loop gain, and in practice R2/R1 is chosen slightly greater than 2 to guarantee start-up (amplitude then limited by a nonlinear network).
condition: Wien-bridge oscillator with equal R and C in the series and parallel arms of the feedback network.
formula: w0 = 1/(C*R) [Eq. 18.12]; R2/R1 = 2 for oscillation [Eq. 18.13]; choose R2/R1 = 2 + delta (small delta) for start-up
erc_rule: In a Wien-bridge topology: fail if R2/R1 <= 2 (will not start) and warn if R2/R1 >> 2 without an amplitude-limiting network (heavy distortion).

statement: A 555 timer wired as a monostable multivibrator produces an output pulse of width T = CR*ln3, approximately 1.1*CR, set entirely by the external R and C (capacitor charges toward VCC until it reaches the internal threshold VTH = 2/3 VCC). (Independently corroborates the Floyd Digital Fundamentals entry: same 1.1·RC factor, here with the ln3 derivation.)
condition: 555 monostable configuration, external timing resistor R to VCC and capacitor C to ground.

statement: A 555 astable multivibrator with charge path RA+RB and discharge path RB oscillates between VTL = 1/3 VCC and VTH = 2/3 VCC with TH = 0.69*C*(RA+RB), TL = 0.69*C*RB, period T = 0.69*C*(RA+2RB), and duty cycle (RA+RB)/(RA+2RB). Duty cycle is always > 50% and approaches 50% only when RA << RB (at the cost of higher supply current).
condition: Standard 555 astable configuration: RA from VCC to discharge pin, RB from discharge pin to the C node.
erc_rule: In a 555 astable: fail any request for duty cycle <= 50% with this standard topology; check chosen RA, RB, C reproduce the requested frequency via T = 0.69*C*(RA+2RB).

source.section: 18.7.3 An Astable Multivibrator Using the 555 IC
